clue.text: Initial blunders by first of presiding officers about Conservative party representative

indicators.note: the first of each of the words presiding and officers is taken, its own heads
the shuffled letters are placed about, around, the abbreviation for Conservative
the word Initial blunders, so its letters go wrong and are rearranged

explanation.surface: Early gaffes by a chairing officer over a Tory party delegate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blunders' rearranges INITIAL to LITIIAN, and 'about' puts it round C to make LITICIAN, after PO from the heads of 'presiding officers'.
explanation.definitionFit: A politician represents a party, standing for election under its banner.

clue.text: Exercises which involve matter raised in newspapers

indicators.note: the upturned matter is placed in the word for newspapers

parts.note: the press is the newspapers collectively

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the word for matter is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: pus is matter discharged from a wound

explanation.surface: Workouts that involve some topic being brought up in the papers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns PUS into SUP, and 'in' puts that inside PRESS; 'matter' means the yellowish discharge, not a subject.
explanation.definitionFit: Press-ups are a familiar gym exercise, pushing the body up from the floor with the arms.

clue.text: Books on railway showing balance

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: Libra is the zodiac sign of the scales, a balance

explanation.surface: Accounts of a train line that reveal its financial balance.
explanation.definitionFit: A library is a collection of books.

clue.text: Gelatinous sweet — translate that into foreign language, please

parts.note: Turkish is the language of Turkey
to delight someone is to please them

explanation.surface: A request to put 'that' into another tongue, labelled as a jelly confection.
explanation.walkthrough: Translating 'please' (DELIGHT) and putting it into a foreign language (TURKISH) gives the sweet; TURKISH DELIGHT is a cubed jelly sweet dusted with sugar.
explanation.definitionFit: This confection is a soft, jelly-like cube of starch and sugar, often rose-flavoured.

clue.text: Aware a gin and tonic's leaving one squiffy

indicators.note: the letter for one is left out of the drink's letters
squiffy means slightly drunk, so the remaining letters reel into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Fully alert, even though a G&T has left someone tipsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' drops I (one) from A GIN TONIC'S and 'squiffy' rearranges the other nine letters; the word 'and' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To be cognisant of something is to be conscious or knowing of it.

clue.text: Expert turning out pedantic, to some extent

indicators.note: turning means the run of letters is read backwards, against the direction of the words
only part of the words out pedantic is used, a stretch running across them

explanation.surface: A specialist who becomes somewhat fussy over details.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to some extent' takes TPEDA from 'ouT PEDAntic' and 'turning' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: An adept is a highly skilled person, a master of some art.

clue.text: Sun article on royal follows Sunday Times leaders

indicators.note: the article and royal pieces come after the leaders
the leaders of Sunday and Times are their opening letters

parts.note: A is the indefinite article
R is a common abbreviation for royal, as in RN

explanation.surface: A tabloid feature on a royal after the headlines of a rival paper.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun and the Sunday Times are British newspapers, a scene that hides the definition: the sun is a star.
explanation.definitionFit: Our sun is the nearest star to Earth.

clue.text: Holidaymaker in French city, one getting lost, ultimately

indicators.note: the letter for one goes in the city's name

parts.note: Tours is a city on the Loire in France
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word lost

explanation.surface: A visitor in a French town, one of whom wanders off in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A tourist is someone travelling for pleasure, on holiday.

clue.text: Overnight flight taken by florid detective

parts.note: florid means flushed, red in the face
an eye, as in private eye, is a detective

explanation.surface: A night plane boarded by a red-faced sleuth.
explanation.definitionFit: A red-eye is a late-night flight that arrives early morning, leaving passengers bleary.

clue.text: Politician linked with Afghans possibly requiring a certain kind of humour?

indicators.note: the politician is joined on to the dogs, with the dogs first

parts.note: Afghan hounds, with long coats, are an example of shaggy dogs
a Tory is a British Conservative politician

explanation.surface: A Conservative MP teamed with long-haired hounds may need a sense of humour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Afghans' looks like people from Afghanistan but means the long-coated hound breed; 'possibly' flags them as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaggy-dog story is a long rambling joke whose humour lies in its pointless punchline.

clue.text: Coal you got at the end of last month?

indicators.note: only what is found at the end of the month's name is kept, its start dropped

parts.note: December is the last month of the year

explanation.surface: What you were left with as the year closed: a last glowing bit of fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing DEC from DECEMBER, the year's final month, leaves its end; 'you got' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An ember is a glowing fragment of coal or wood left in a dying fire.

clue.text: Runner gives reason after entering English youth hostel

indicators.note: the English youth hostel pieces go into the word for reason

parts.note: a ground is a reason, as in grounds for complaint
YH is the abbreviation for youth hostel

explanation.surface: An athlete explains why after checking into a hostel in England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' suggests an athlete but means a racing dog.
explanation.definitionFit: Greyhounds are dogs bred for racing, run on tracks.

clue.text: Know Glaswegian man's name

definitions.meaning: in Scottish speech, as in Glasgow
a short form of Kenneth, a male first name

explanation.definitionFit: Scots use this word for know, as in 'd'ye ken', and it is also a familiar boy's name.

clue.text: Indian mystic American's seen in Westr inster

indicators.note: the American's abbreviation is seen inside the postcode

parts.note: SW1 is the London postcode district of Westminster, with 1 read as I
AM is an abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: An Indian holy man from the US turns up in the seat of British government.
explanation.walkthrough: Westminster, home of Parliament, has the postcode SW1; read the 1 as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A swami is a Hindu religious teacher or ascetic.

clue.text: Honesty: one encounters it amongst refined gentry

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the word it is placed amongst the reworked gentry letters
refined means processed, so the letters of gentry are reworked

explanation.surface: Truthfulness: a person meets it among the cultured upper classes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'refined' rearranges GENTRY to NTEGRY, and 'amongst' puts IT inside it, after I for one.
explanation.definitionFit: Integrity is uprightness, being truthful and principled.

clue.text: Shrinks, at length?

parts.note: shrink is a slang shortening; the full-length form of the word for these psychiatrists is wanted

explanation.definitionFit: Shrinks is slang for therapists, short for headshrinkers, and the full professional title names those who analyse the mind.

clue.text: Stars, with agreement from Russians, entering European capital

indicators.note: the Russian agreement is entered after the capital

parts.note: and means with, plus
Rome is the capital of Italy
da is Russian for yes

explanation.surface: Constellations, with Russian approval, arriving in an Italian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Andromeda is a constellation, a group of stars, home to a famous galaxy.

clue.text: A plea for help about most advisable heat-resistant material?

indicators.note: the distress call goes about, around, the word for most advisable

parts.note: SOS is the international distress signal
best means most advisable, as in it is best to wait

explanation.surface: A cry for help over the ideal fireproof stuff.
explanation.definitionFit: Asbestos is a fibrous mineral used for fireproofing, now banned as a health hazard.

clue.text: What may appear to be opening remarks?

definitions.text: What may appear to be opening remarks?

parts.words: What may appear to be opening remarks?
parts.note: punctuation printed at the start of spoken words opens them, so it opens a remark

explanation.definitionFit: Quotation marks, the first of a pair, appear at the start of quoted speech.

clue.text: Air route African runner's taken into Holland, not Switzerland

indicators.note: the trimmed bird goes into the abbreviation for Holland

parts.note: NL is the international code for the Netherlands, Holland

indicators.note: not Switzerland means its abbreviation is taken out of the bird

parts.note: the ostrich is a flightless African bird that runs fast
CH is the international code for Switzerland

explanation.surface: A flight path for a runner from Africa brought to the Netherlands, bypassing the Swiss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' drops CH from OSTRICH to leave OSTRI, which 'taken into' puts inside NL; 'Air route' is a passage for breathing, not flights.
explanation.definitionFit: A nostril is an opening through which air passes into the nose.

clue.text: Further story's penned by French writer

indicators.note: penned means enclosed, so the story sits inside the word for further

parts.note: more means further, additional
a story is a lie, a fib

explanation.surface: An extra tale written by a French author.
explanation.definitionFit: Molière was a 17th-century French playwright, author of Tartuffe.

clue.text: Low-tech item you can count on?

definitions.text: Low-tech item you can count on?

parts.words: Low-tech item you can count on?
parts.note: count on is read as reckoning numbers on a device of beads, not trusting something

explanation.definitionFit: An abacus is a frame of beads on wires used for arithmetic.

clue.text: Review DA obtains, suggesting some form of torture

indicators.note: review means look at again, recast, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A prosecutor's report hints at cruel punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: DA is a US district attorney in the surface; 'Review' rearranges DA plus OBTAINS.
explanation.definitionFit: The bastinado is a punishment of beating the soles of the feet.

clue.text: A ring road traffic accident, leading to main artery

parts.note: O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A crash on the ring road leads to a big trunk road.
explanation.definitionFit: The aorta is the largest artery, carrying blood from the heart.

clue.text: Dicky loves to do crosswords

indicators.note: dicky means shaky or unsound, so the letters of loves are disordered

explanation.surface: Someone called Dicky likes doing puzzles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dicky' looks like a name but means unreliable.
explanation.definitionFit: To work out a crossword is to find its answers.

clue.text: Police must be satisfied

definitions.meaning: a demand that is ... is satisfied

explanation.definitionFit: London's Metropolitan force is called this for short, and a need fulfilled has been this.

clue.text: Big drawer containing orchestra's bits and pieces

indicators.note: the orchestra is broken into bits and reassembled in another order

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A huge set of storage holding a band's assorted items.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawer' suggests furniture but means something that draws, pulls a cart.
explanation.definitionFit: A carthorse is a big strong horse bred to draw heavy loads.

clue.text: Past tense required, that's evident

parts.note: over means finished, past
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A grammar note: the past tense is needed, plainly.
explanation.definitionFit: Something overt is open and plain to see.

clue.text: Recalled being involved in cricket last season

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the letters are read backwards
the letters are involved in the words cricket last, running across them

explanation.surface: Remembered playing cricket in the previous summer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being involved in' takes TLAS from 'crickeT LASt' and 'Recalled' reverses it; 'season' is the verb, to flavour.
explanation.definitionFit: To season food is to flavour it, most simply with sodium chloride.

clue.text: Cartel says there are problems with pollution reducing devices

indicators.note: problems with the words mean their letters are disturbed into another order

explanation.surface: A business group admits trouble with its emissions equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: Catalytic converters in car exhausts cut harmful emissions.
